## 固定收益市場主軸

美國公債週四反彈，10年期殖利率結束連續八個交易日上升的走勢。油價回落，加上英國公債強勁回升，緩解全球借款成本壓力；美國10年期指標殖利率收低7個基點至4.94%，2年期也下降7個基點至4.67%。聯準會表明對抗通膨的立場後，投資人開始找到買進債券的空間，但並未放棄進一步緊縮的預期。

當天最出乎市場意料的政策來自英國：英國央行維持政策利率不變，卻暫停出售公債，並取消原定的長天期債券出售計畫。美國數據對債市反彈的支持則不一致，失業救濟申請人數偏低、製造業價格壓力增強，抵銷了營建疲弱的訊號。融資市場依然活絡，花旗完成歷來最大規模的美元債發行，新一批AI相關融資則考驗在利率仍高之際，投資人願意為合約收入與未來成長支付多少價格。

## 美債反彈，就業與房市訊號分歧

各天期美國附息公債全面上漲，5年期殖利率下跌8個基點至4.78%，30年期下降6個基點至5.29%。2年與10年期利差維持27個基點，先前市場重新反映緊縮預期所形成的較平坦曲線並未逆轉。2年期殖利率本週仍上升11個基點，近一個月上升48個基點；10年期本週下降1個基點，近一個月仍上升22個基點。

油價連續第二天下跌，是債市回升的助力。紐約下午5時固定收益市場收盤時，布蘭特原油每桶$104.08，下跌1.65%；西德州原油為$101.19，下跌1.21%。交易仍反映市場對沙烏地阿拉伯先前宣布部分輸油管線恢復運作的期待，希望藉此紓解交運限制。即使布蘭特近一個月仍上漲14.54%，供應可望改善的前景依然支持各類金融資產價格。RBC Capital Markets的Blake Gwinn表示，油價已成為左右30年期美債殖利率的主要因素，而且兩者關係愈來愈有自我強化的傾向。

花旗分析師Michael Chang也認為，市場相信聯準會會應對通膨持續的風險，改善了債市氣氛。不過，週四收盤的殖利率拆解顯示，當天直接下降的是實質借款成本：10年期抗通膨公債（TIPS）殖利率下降7個基點至2.61%，同天期損益兩平通膨率則維持2.33%。名目指標殖利率的跌幅因此全數對應實質殖利率的下降。通膨補償本週已下降7個基點，但週四收盤並未再降。

相較於名目公債的反彈，新發行抗通膨債券的需求較弱。財政部增額標售$190億10年期TIPS，得標殖利率為2.653%，較下午1時投標截止前的標售前交易殖利率高約2個基點，顯示買方要求額外補償才願意承接。這是2008年以來最高的標售殖利率，上次為2.438%；然而，油價回落與聯準會可能繼續升息，降低了當天通膨避險工具的吸引力。

就業數據並不支持近期即將寬鬆的看法。截至9月12日當週，首次申請失業救濟人數減少1萬人至19.6萬人，為7月中旬以來最低，也低於路透調查預估的20.8萬人；四週移動平均減少2,750人至20萬3,250人。截至9月5日當週，續領人數減少3.9萬人至173.0萬人，低於預估的178.0萬人，前值經修正為176.9萬人。續領人數創2024年1月以來最低，但路透指出，季節調整的扭曲可能影響數據。

費城聯準銀行9月調查顯示，製造業仍快速擴張，但細項透露的訊息較令人擔憂。整體活動指數由47.4降至37.8，仍高於市場預估的30.5；新訂單由30.1降至29.2，出貨維持27.7，就業則從27.9降至11.8，平均每週工時指數為18.0。企業活動只是擴張減速，並未全面萎縮，但雇用動能已明顯落後整體活動。

價格指標反而上升：投入價格由40.9升至48.6，銷售價格上升約14點至31.3，為4月以來最高。未來活動指數由73.6降至52.9，資本支出指數由48.20降至37.10，但未來投入價格與銷售價格指數分別升至71.3及72.3。9月7日至15日蒐集的回覆也顯示，72%的企業面臨至少輕微的勞動供給限制，高於6月的50%；36%預期未來三個月能源限制將惡化。這份調查呈現成長動能放緩與成本壓力增強並存，不能單純視為有助通膨下降的景氣降溫。

房市則更清楚顯示緊縮的影響。8月新屋開工月減2.6%，年率為127.5萬戶，低於預估的131.0萬戶，主要受多戶住宅營建大幅下滑拖累。前月開工年率上修至130.9萬戶，7月月減幅修正為9%。營建許可初值由143.3萬戶下降2.7%至139.4萬戶，低於預估的141.0萬戶，也逆轉前月4.3%的增幅。營建活動與後續動工的許可數量雙雙轉弱。

成屋簽約僅小幅改善。全美不動產經紀人協會（NAR）待完成銷售指數上升0.3%至71.2，是5月以來首次增加，7月則經修正為下降2.6%。結果優於彭博調查預估的下降0.1%，但不及Trading Economics另列的市場共識成長2%。銷售仍較去年同期減少4.7%，前次年減幅為2.2%。規模最大的南部增加2.3%，西部也改善，中西部與東北部則下降。NAR首席經濟學家Lawrence Yun表示，儘管房貸利率上升，買方仍持續簽約，但交易活動依舊低迷。

最新房地美調查顯示，融資門檻又提高：30年期房貸利率由6.76%升至6.95%，15年期由6.09%升至6.26%。每週房貸利率上升，與當日美債反彈同時存在，因為後者僅回吐此前殖利率漲幅的一部分。這也有助解釋，為何簽約略有起色，尚未帶動更廣泛的營建復甦。

儘管殖利率偏高，市場波動卻相對平靜。路透報導，10年期美元利率的三個月選擇權隱含年化波動約79.5個基點，低於2023年10月指標美債殖利率接近5%時的約134個基點。巴克萊策略師Amrut Nashikkar認為，近期拋售主要反映成長轉強、市場預期由降息轉向升息，以及長期政策利率預期提高，而非擔憂美債需求。選擇權需求較集中於短期利率，因為聯準會如何回應仍有較大不確定性。

對週四這波反彈能否持續，各家看法分歧。BMO Capital Markets的Ian Lyngen預期經濟數據將重新主導市場，未來幾週殖利率可望下滑。KKR則將年底10年期殖利率預估由5.0%上調至5.1%，2027年底預估由4.7%上調至4.9%。Henry McVey團隊仍預期聯準會於12月及3月升息，但考量通膨持續、名目成長、財政赤字及資金競爭，現在認為利率將維持在升息後水準至2029年初，而非原先預估的2028年。

Christian Mueller-Glissman領導的高盛策略團隊認為，較高的起始殖利率改善了債券長期的利息收益吸引力，但能源與政策衝擊仍可能使債券短期內無法可靠地抵銷股票風險。DoubleLine的Jeffrey Gundlach在紐約一場活動提出更嚴峻的情境：衰退可能使赤字升至GDP的12%，年度利息支出增至約$3兆，迫使當局干預長期利率。他認為殖利率若達約6.5%，可能促成類似扭轉操作的措施，也提及削減票息的可能性，同時承認這種債務重整將損害未來借款能力。

週四其他市場反映的則是眼前壓力緩解。標普500上漲1.14%，那斯達克100上漲1.73%，半導體股上漲3.14%；VIX降至15.44，美元指數小跌0.07%。實質殖利率與能源價格下降，減輕估值面臨的兩項壓力，帶動股債同步回升。

## 英國調整公債供給，歐洲持續辯論通膨風險

英國央行的調整遠超市場原先對年度量化緊縮速度的預期。央行將所有公債出售暫停至2027年4月，停止原定的長天期債券出售，並規劃於2034年9月結束量化緊縮。即使貨幣政策委員會警告可能必須升息，這項宣布仍立即移除一項市場供給來源。

方案將£4,880億的債券組合分為三部分：2049年或之後到期的約£1,200億將保留，作為流通紙鈔的資產支持；2035年及以前到期的另£2,220億將隨到期自然縮減；其餘2035年至2049年間到期的£1,460億，則以每年約£200億出售，可能由英國債務管理局（DMO）承接，而非直接賣入市場。移轉條件仍須研議並由財政部決定，暫停出售正好提供處理時間。

這不只是縮小出售規模。DMO若買進並註銷這些債券，可改發更符合需求天期的債券。前英國央行決策官員Michael Saunders表示，以流動性較佳的指標券發行，取代央行出售流動性較差的非指標券，可能更持久地降低借款成本。方案下平均每年資產縮減為£460億，其中主動出售£200億，低於預算責任辦公室原先假設的每年主動出售£320億。

英國公債因而扭轉稍早跌勢。決策後的市場報導顯示，30年期殖利率下降12個基點至5.74%，為5月以來最大跌幅；2年期下降6個基點至4.70%。交易員將未來一年升息預期下修至不到四次、每次25個基點。英債回升也支持其他歐洲債券，當日報導中的德國10年期殖利率下跌約3個基點至3.48%。

財政影響則比市場的即時反應複雜。央行先前創造的£1,240億獲利已由歷屆政府支用；自2022年起，財政部承諾賠付的量化緊縮損失已達£1,100億，央行原本還預估將再虧損£1,000億。總裁貝利表示，現任政府上台前就已討論這項改制，貨幣政策獨立性將獲保留。一名知悉財政部評估的人士表示，財政部認為改變對財政大臣John Healey於10月28日提出的預算案影響不大，但可能略為壓縮主要財政規則下的緩衝空間。

利率方面，貨幣政策委員會以6票對3票維持3.75%不變。貝利表示，能源衝擊至今對英國薪資與物價的影響有限，但若持續下去，升息的可能性就會提高。央行現在預估明年初通膨約4%，並將第三季成長預測上調至0.4%。會議紀錄警告，能源的間接影響可能只是延後出現，而非變小，食品與AI相關產品需求也帶來額外的上行風險。

Catherine Mann、Megan Greene及Huw Pill再次主張立即升息，尤其擔憂預估中的物價加速，恰逢年初數百萬勞工協商薪資的時期。支持不變的多數委員中，Swati Dhingra與Alan Taylor強調勞動市場仍有閒置、金融條件偏緊。Taylor指出，目前殖利率曲線高於2022至2023年週期，當時通膨接近7%。減少公債供給與維持政策利率處理的是不同問題：前者紓解市場壓力，後者則反映委員對輸入型通膨是否正轉為國內持續性通膨，尚有歧見。

歐洲央行官員的新談話呈現類似區別，但沒有新的政策決議。愛爾蘭的Gabriel Makhlouf表示，10月29日會議仍可能採取行動，既不認同也不排除投資人對進一步升息的預期。他認為目前2.5%的存款利率落在中性區間，尚未看到令人擔憂的薪資帶動第二輪效應，但強調能源衝擊仍在持續，通膨風險偏向上行。

芬蘭的Olli Rehn也表示薪資成長溫和，迄今沒有物價與薪資螺旋上升，同時認為上週升息有其必要。他強調，金融市場已帶來的緊縮是政策重要考量，並警告普遍性消費補貼可能削弱能源轉型誘因。Rehn支持歐洲共同舉債支應國防，並表示ECB備有TPI與OMT等工具以維護貨幣政策傳導，但目前沒有動用必要。

克羅埃西亞的Ante Zigman更重視通膨失控最終損害成長的風險。他表示，第二季活動優於預期，使決策者有理由專注物價穩定，但也承認薪資與非能源通膨仍受控制。他不認同ECB已進入其不利情境的看法，並表示10月討論將依數據而定，不會追隨市場要求積極緊縮的聲音。這些個別談話顯示，官員共同關切通膨持續性，但對行動時點仍保有不同判斷。

捷克央行一致決議維持利率3.75%。總裁Ales Michl表示，6月升息就目前而言已帶來足夠緊縮，11月仍將在維持與升息之間選擇。除了能源風險，他也點出服務價格、住房、薪資及舉債支應的政府支出；雖然8月整體通膨低於目標，核心通膨持續偏高仍需要維持緊縮。遠期利率協議反映今年還會升息約兩次、未來12個月約四次，每次25個基點。Michl表示國內市場利率深受美國政策影響，未認可這條升息路徑。

食品價格也帶來新的通膨風險。摩根大通經濟學家預測，全球食品通膨將由2026年上半年的2.8%升至2027年上半年的5%；聯合國一項食品商品指數已來到2022年底以來最高。Carmignac的Marie-Anne Allier預期，天候、肥料限制與航運中斷將造成緩慢但持續的供給衝擊。能源與氣候情報中心（ECIU）新分析估計，酷熱與乾旱可能使歐洲及英國馬鈴薯收成減少約350萬噸，按目前價格計算，農民損失超過€8億；報導中的產量減損幅度，比利時為21%、法國13%、德國10%。

摩根資產管理的Karen Ward提出重要的相反觀點：必需品變貴會壓低其他消費，歐美勞動市場未必能支撐持續的薪資轉嫁。油價當日雖回落，央行仍擔心供給壓力的持續時間與擴散範圍，兩種判斷的區別因此重要。

貿易政策則帶來另一項潛在成本衝擊。川普威脅，若歐盟擬與加拿大建立的聯繫不利美國利益，將對歐洲貿易加徵關稅或施加限制；卡尼週四在歐洲議會演說時則歡迎更密切的關係。美國國會也最終通過法案，授予對俄羅斯石油買家課徵關稅的新權力。兩項發展都尚未確立新稅率。另據知情人士，美國針對產能過剩的關稅公告，預計延至川習峰會之後，最終稅率仍不確定。

## 銀行發債需求強勁，AI企業拓展融資管道

美債殖利率回落改善發行條件，花旗以歷來最大規模美元債交易籌得$120億，訂單高峰約$400億。其中11年期券吸引約$180億需求，為各券別之冠，最終利差為高於指標0.93個百分點，低於最初洽談的約1.25個百分點。

富國銀行也完成$60億發行，包含4年及11年期券，訂單高峰約$280億。兩筆交易使美國六大銀行今年投資級債發行總額升至$1,773億；花旗累計$183億、富國$240億，相較之下高盛為$440億。週四共有六筆高評級債發行，當週規模接近承銷商原先預期。

花旗需求集中於最長天期券，再次顯示只要發行人利差可接受，投資人仍願意承接較長天期債券。借款人不願鎖定昂貴的長期資金，讓投資人競逐有限的長天期供給。週四交易說明，只要公債殖利率回落，且投資人仍願意承擔企業風險，聯準會提高利率不一定會使初級市場關閉。

美國高收益債利差當天小幅收窄，投資級債基金LQD報酬約0.68%，HYG上漲0.38%，新興市場債券基金EMB上漲0.64%。已發行債券價格回升的同時，AI基礎設施借款人的融資條件仍有明顯差異。

CoreWeave啟動擬議的$30億優先可轉換債發行，2033年到期，並可增額$5億；初步票息區間為2.375%至2.875%。募集資金將用於一般公司用途及與交易相關的衍生工具協議。摩根士丹利、高盛、摩根大通及富國銀行參與承作，預計週四稍晚定價。

公司同時設立按市價發行股票計畫，允許分次出售最多3,500萬股，並表示這種彈性有助信用體質朝投資級靠攏。可轉換債搭配潛在增發股票，讓融資來源不再只限傳統貸款與債券。今年美國上市公司透過可轉換證券籌資已達創紀錄的$1,373億，全球AI相關公司借款則約$4,190億。

CleanSpark為喬治亞州桑德斯維爾資料中心，尋求首次發行約$22.3億高收益債。5年期券初步洽談殖利率約8.5%，比彭博追蹤的BB級債平均高約2個百分點；週四啟動時，訂單約等於發行規模，預計週五定價。摩根士丹利主辦融資，高盛與富國銀行也參與承銷。

該專案已依$66億、20年期合約，全數出租予Meta子公司Anviran，租金及營運費用由Meta擔保，預計2027年第四季啟用。長約提供長期收入承諾，但在設施完工營運、租金開始支應營運之前，投資人仍要求營建融資提供可觀的殖利率補償。這是美國首次與Meta資料中心相關的非投資級債發行；今年開發商已發行約$390億高收益債，其中不少有超大規模雲端業者租約支持。

亞洲的晶片採購也帶來新增借款需求。據知悉洽談的人士，輝達合作夥伴GMI Cloud正與銀行及私募信貸基金討論$3億貸款，用來替泰國一座設施採購處理器，運算容量將供騰訊使用。這筆潛在融資的授信評估焦點，是建物內的設備。

隨投資而來的電力需求，也讓融資擴展至科技發行人之外。彭博新能源財經週四公布的研究顯示，銀行2025年安排及承銷的能源業交易達$2.3兆，比2024年增加15%。低碳融資增加16%，創五年高點，石油、天然氣及煤炭交易則成長13%。研究反映前一年的融資情況，各地差異顯著，華爾街銀行在低碳融資方面落後歐洲同業。

AI以外，必勝客正籌備以加盟費支持的債券，為LongRange Capital的$15億收購提供融資。收購已於本月稍早完成，瑞銀提供資金，預計在信評機構評估債務後主辦整體業務證券化，目前尚未啟動發行。這種結構把質押的營運現金流隔離於特殊目的公司，可降低融資成本，但餐飲營運表現仍然重要：FAT Brands在部分整體業務證券化債務未能付息後，於1月聲請破產，其此類債務合計$12億。

## 債務協商揭露現金流與估值落差

Braskem重整談判惡化。債券持有人要求股東先作出可強制履行的增資承諾，否則反對先投入約$20億新資金。爭議涉及$110億債務，其中約$70億欠債券持有人，司法重整因此重新進入談判議題。

8月底提出的方案擬以約$12.5億債權人資金，按最高面額50%的價格買回既有債務，另留$7.5億作為營運資金，與最初未考慮減記本金的討論不同。Petrobras與IG4 Capital弱化注資承諾的措辭後，債權人提出反對，有些甚至考慮不再提出反提案。據知情人士，Petrobras希望避免Braskem破產，但未提出貸方要求的約束性承諾；部分債權人已不認為可能的後續股權發行足以解決問題。

各方須於10月9日前就條款書達成共識，Braskem則須在11月底前取得過半債權人支持的最終計畫。公司2030年到期美元債殖利率約26%。眼前障礙在於誰能提供確實可得的新資本，而不只是既有債務能展延多久。

澳洲建商Bathla已無力清償債務，Centuria Bass Credit正探詢出售部分對該公司的債權。據知悉討論的人士，潛在買方要求至少20%至30%的折價，目前並無交易即將成交，管理公司也不評論可能折價幅度。公司先前揭露持有A$2.78億Bathla債務，以維多利亞州及新南威爾斯州六個住宅專案作擔保，並已暫停兩檔基金贖回。

Bathla積欠約A$34億，大多數債權人為私募信貸業者。管理人Teneo已取得約A$400萬緊急融資，正尋求更大規模方案。營建及借款成本提高，同時銷售與房價走弱，使債權能否出售取決於外部買方願付的價格。所議折價是對債權部位的出價，並非已確定的回收價值。

法國不動產服務公司Emeria的債務討論則牽涉獲利定義。公司將代理式AI預計於未來兩年提升效率、節省的€2,000萬，計入截至6月30日的過去12個月EBITDA。Emeria表示，這些是文件製作、客服、會計及後勤自動化方面已辨識的措施，符合與貸方議定的方法；該調整尚未經獨立會計師查核或核閱，仍可能改變。

公司公布的槓桿約為擬制調整後EBITDA的8.44倍。彭博計算，若排除AI調整及其他數項、合計約€4,000萬的調整，倍數較接近9.3倍。Emeria負債約€35億，在獲利走弱、到期日逼近之際，正討論由財務贊助股東可能注資€3.5億。Spread Research的Benjamin Sabahi主張，AI節省應在真正產生後才計入；其他市場人士則認為與一般營運效率調整相似。Emeria強調各項調整均分別揭露，讓貸方自行判斷。

私募信貸困境指標的新比較，同樣顯示定義的重要性。Houlihan Lokey按貸款規模加權的違約指標仍低於1%，反映最大型借款人持續履約；Pimco針對約$5,000億美國企業發展公司（BDC）市場的影子違約指標卻達19%，高於2022年的約14%。後者納入貸款承作後、為紓解現金流壓力才增訂的以債付息（PIK）條款，不包括融資之初就約定的PIK。

定義不同，部分解釋了Pimco指標與先前公布的惠譽6.3%違約率，以及Lincoln International歐洲貸款1.5%指標之間的落差；Lincoln排除了部分此類事件。Credit Benchmark研究另指出，過去兩年BDC平均風險下降5%，其底層持倉的違約風險卻上升12%。Pimco的Lotfi Karoui表示，單看停止認列利息收入的貸款指標，可能漏掉那些延後認列壓力的債務重整。各研究涵蓋的借款人與事件不同，但共同顯示，持續計提利息可以與償還能力惡化並存。

ING策略師Timothy Rahill估計，管理人在高槓桿投資組合中可承受8%至9%的違約率，但重大衝擊後若升至12%至15%，就會引發系統性疑慮。這是他對潛在損失承受能力的判斷，與Pimco涵蓋較廣的貸款修改指標不同。協商、延後支付與正式違約，即使被歸於同一類困境，對現金的影響也不一樣。

基金流動性另有兩項進展。9月以來，規模約$36億的Schwab Municipal Bond ETF流出超過$5.3億，其中上週某日流出創紀錄的$3.6億。嘉信持有略逾半數基金股份，使彭博行業研究的Eric Balchunas懷疑是模型投資組合再平衡所致。即使美債利率上升與大量供給已壓抑免稅債券，這個解釋仍有別於市政債信用普遍惡化。

土耳其監管機關則從先前的贖回中斷，進一步規劃清算Tera Portfoy等業者管理的約$200億基金。當局就涉嫌操縱股價提出刑事告發並祭出交易禁令，部分主管遭拘留，另一些遭限制出境。Tera管理約7,300億土耳其里拉，相當於$150億，部分受影響基金集中持有流動性不足的股票。大盤在連續三天下跌近10%後止穩，但清算已使這些持股如何出售，成為當地市場必須實際面對的問題。

## 主權融資與亞洲政策各循不同路徑

印度央行完成已宣布售債計畫的首批5,000億印度盧比操作，使原本預期的流動性回收正式落實。這是2017年11月以來首次透過標售進行公開市場淨售債，涵蓋2029至2032年到期券，截止價格介於102.25至105.63印度盧比，吸收了接近銀行體系存款0.2%的資金。

結果公布後，5年期殖利率一度上升6個基點至6.83%，超過指標10年期最多3個基點的升幅。銀行先前以剩餘流動性買債，較短天期受惠最多，資金回收時也更易受影響。路透報導，剩餘流動性由9月6日創紀錄的11.6兆印度盧比降至7.4兆，繳稅資金流出與外匯干預也促成下降。10月7日政策檢討前，9月21日及28日還各安排2,500億印度盧比售債。

印度也在研議如何拓展長期融資。印度證券交易委員會（SEBI）主席Tuhin Kanta Pandey延續5月諮詢內容，支持地方政府聯合借款，協助較小城鎮進入債市。NaBFID主管Rajkiran Rai G.表示，到2031財年，城市基礎設施需求可能達82兆至86兆印度盧比，約$8,550億至$9,000億。截至3月底止年度，累計僅22個地方機構透過31筆市政債發行籌得逾450億印度盧比。Pandey強調，要擴大市場，必須具備信用、治理、資訊揭露與可靠的專案現金流。

馬來西亞面臨的融資壓力不同：相對日本公債的殖利率優勢正在縮小。10年期主權債相對同天期日本公債的殖利率溢酬已壓縮至約112個基點，低於五年平均278個基點。截至2025年底，日本投資人持有¥1.1兆馬來西亞債券，創2014年有紀錄以來新高，占其亞洲債券持倉13%。聯昌國際銀行的Michelle Chia表示，日本公債殖利率上升，提高持有海外債券的機會成本，也加大資金回流日本的風險。

國內重新定價進一步加重壓力。馬來西亞利率交換已反映未來一年緊縮近50個基點，8月底時還不到25個基點；10年期殖利率自6月以來已上升51個基點。當局週四又宣布發行50億馬來西亞令吉、2033年到期債券。法國巴黎銀行的Chandresh Jain指出，燃料補貼增加、成長強勁及通膨風險，疊加了供給與外部利率壓力。

日本本身的融資基礎也出現明顯變化。4月至9月零售日本公債銷售創紀錄達¥5.14兆，年增84%。家戶持有¥1,132兆現金及存款，公債持倉僅相當於該金額的1.9%。彭博比較估計，若回到2008年4.5%的高峰比率，可能意味著另有¥28.5兆買盤，相當於本財年政府發債量22%；這是潛在資產配置移轉，而非家戶已承諾購買。

零售公債最低申購額為¥1萬，殖利率高於定存、但低於相近的可交易日本公債。財務省計畫今年稍晚將申購資格擴大至非營利法人與小型未上市公司；財務大臣片山皋月提議將公債納入NISA，另有提交參議院的法案擬讓部分零售公債免徵遺產稅。巴克萊的門田真一郎表示，日本央行縮減購債之際，家戶需求增加可減少機構投資人必須承接的供給。

首相高市早苗在週四內閣改組中，留任片山皋月及經濟再生大臣城內實。城內承諾更清楚地說明公共財政，並表示政府追求更強成長，不等於無節制擴張財政。這項說明伴隨財政與匯率政策主管留任，並非新的支出方案。

其他亞洲經濟體則有理由不機械式跟隨美國緊縮。泰國央行助理總裁Don Nakornthab表示，在經濟疲弱之際，1.00%的政策利率已屬高度寬鬆，所有選項仍開放。他維持2026年2.3%、2027年1.8%的成長預測，預期第三季成長超過3%，第四季放緩至約2%。今年平均通膨預估約2%，低於6月預估的2.8%，出口成長則可能超過央行14%的預測。他認為聯準會行動沒有明顯即時影響，也無須跟進。

新加坡8月電子出口年增132%，其中個人電腦增加238%、磁碟機214%、積體電路91%。巴克萊將2026及2027年成長預測各上調1個百分點至5.5%及4%，但經濟學家Brian Tan預估核心通膨僅1.7%。他認為，這波資本密集型產業繁榮主要靠提高產能利用率，而非增加雇用；外商也較可能匯回利潤，而非在當地大幅加薪。

Tan預期新加坡金融管理局僅會因商品與天候風險再小幅緊縮，維持不變也有相當可能。馬來亞銀行的蔡學敏與Brian Lee預期，繼4月及7月調整後，10月不會再變動；兩次調整合計使政策匯率區間斜率提高約75個基點。華僑銀行的Selena Ling表示，若要再採取行動，可能需要看到2027年核心通膨展望有上行風險。出口數據推升了成長預測，但經濟學家對國內物價壓力也會隨之增強，並無同等共識。

中國低成本融資管道持續提供替代選擇。香港綠色金融協會主席馬駿在新訪談中表示，前八個月中國大陸熊貓債發行約人民幣2,000億元。他以巴基斯坦票息2.5%的熊貓債為例，說明綠色專案的融資優勢，並明確指出該債有亞洲基礎設施投資銀行與亞洲開發銀行擔保。他也介紹新推出的香港綠色加速器，旨在協助開發中經濟體準備具融資條件的專案，參與者包括亞投行、絲路基金、GenZero與滙豐。這項倡議不只著眼於資本，也重視專案前期準備；馬駿估計，新興市場當地銀行拒絕了90%的綠色專案提案。

其他市場的主權美元債表現高度取決於各國情況。莫三比克債券9月報酬約3%，塞內加爾為2.2%，相較之下新興市場債券指數虧損1.23%。週四倫敦下午2時20分，莫三比克$9億、2031年到期債券殖利率為10.43%，本月下降76個基點，為2022年4月以來最低。Aquila的Manuel Mondia將表現歸因於與IMF談判的氣氛、與中國討論債務重新安排，以及初步的債券持有人重整提議。

渣打銀行的Samir Gadio表示，塞內加爾確認暫時繼續償債，並支付2048年到期債券票息後，債券出現回升。總統Bassirou Diomaye Faye已於週二與IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva會面，但$22億方案仍待IMF董事會批准。付款與協商的新進展支持債券價格收復部分失土，但外債問題仍未解決。

秘魯總統Keiko Fujimori請求央行總裁Julio Velarde留任後，參議院確認其再任五年。這使自2006年以來的貨幣領導延續，消除眼前的接班不確定性。加拿大則出售C$30億、2059年6月1日到期債券，平均殖利率4.201%，創2007年7月以來加拿大30年期標售最高。即使當日全球債價改善，這筆完成的標售仍顯示鎖定長期資金的成本居高不下。

歐盟執委會著眼的是需求，而非標售條件，承諾推動歐盟債券納入主要主權債指數。執委Valdis Dombrovskis表示，儘管流通餘額約€8,000億，次級市場流動性也可比歐洲大型主權發行人，未納入指數仍限制需求與流動性。這些債券在結算機構及ECB再融資操作中，已享有與主權債相同的擔保品待遇。隨共同借款擴大，包括與下期歐盟長期預算相關的融資，更廣泛的指數認可將更重要，但目前仍是政策目標，尚未完成指數調整。

## 後續市場觀察重點

日本央行9月18日決策是最近的政策考驗。彭博調查的所有經濟學家都預期，利率將由1.00%升至1.25%，總裁植田和男記者會訂於日本時間下午3時30分。焦點因而在於，他會將這次行動定位為後續持續加快升息，還是單次加速。升至1.25%將進入日本央行估計的中性利率區間下緣；若仍形容金融條件寬鬆，就會為進一步緊縮保留空間。高市任命的淺田統一郎與佐藤綾野如何投票，也有助判斷支持程度。

這番指引面對的是更高的美國利率路徑，以及日圓再次承壓的局面。SMBC日興的丸山凜斗認為，若市場解讀偏鴿，美元兌日圓可能走向158；ACCM的Glenn Yin則警告，若日本央行令人失望，不能排除160。近期投機性日圓空單減少，以及可能再次干預匯市，則是制衡因素。對債市而言，日本家戶需求增加，搭配馬來西亞殖利率溢酬大幅縮小，使日本國內與海外債券的相對吸引力格外重要。

美國9月18日公布工業生產，將接續檢驗費城調查中活動減速、成本上升的組合。市場預估8月工業生產增加0.3%，前值0.2%；製造業產出也預期增加0.3%，產能利用率由76.3%升至76.4%。Michelle Bowman當天預定發表談話，可用來了解最新就業與製造業證據如何影響政策判斷。9月22日ADP每週就業估計及9月23日標普全球綜合PMI初值，將進一步提供最新雇用與更廣泛的活動調查。

能源風險仍可能中斷這波壓力緩解。川普告訴Axios，在下週於聯合國與波斯灣國家領袖會晤前，他正接近就是否再次攻擊伊朗作出決定。摩根大通石油分析師表示，衝突走向終結的路徑愈來愈難預測。再次升級的威脅與週四油價回落形成對照，而英國央行新通膨預測及費城調查說明，高成本持續多久的重要性，遠超過下一次油價單日漲跌。

CleanSpark預計週五定價，將直接檢驗一個仍在營建、租金由Meta擔保的專案，能否按初步洽談的8.5%殖利率融資。Braskem的10月9日條款書期限則考驗另一個問題：股東是否願意作出金額足夠、具有約束力的出資承諾，讓重整不必進入法院。英國財政部還須決定擬議中向DMO移轉債券的操作方式；安排確定後，才能判斷週四英債的即時反彈，有多少會轉化為投資人所承接債券天期與流動性的持久改變。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied on Thursday, ending an eight-session rise in the 10-year yield as cheaper oil and a sharp recovery in British government bonds relieved pressure on global borrowing costs. The U.S. benchmark finished 7 basis points lower at 4.94%, while the 2-year fell by the same amount to 4.67%. Investors found room to buy bonds after the Federal Reserve's inflation-fighting message without abandoning expectations of further tightening.

Britain supplied the day's clearest policy surprise: the Bank of England paused gilt sales and abandoned long-dated disposals while keeping its policy rate unchanged. U.S. data were less uniformly supportive of the bond rally, with low unemployment claims and firmer manufacturing prices offsetting weak construction. Financing markets remained active. Citigroup completed a record dollar sale, and new AI-related offerings tested how much investors would pay for contracted revenues and prospective growth at still-elevated interest rates.

## Treasuries Recover as Labor and Housing Diverge

The Treasury advance extended across the coupon curve. The 5-year yield fell 8 basis points to 4.78%, and the 30-year declined 6 basis points to 5.29%. The 2s10s spread held at 27 basis points, preserving the flatter shape established during the preceding tightening repricing rather than reversing it. The 2-year remained 11 basis points higher over the week and 48 higher over the month; the 10-year was down 1 basis point over the week but still up 22 over the month.

Oil's second daily decline helped the recovery. At the 5 p.m. New York fixed-income close, Brent stood at $104.08 a barrel, down 1.65%, and WTI at $101.19, down 1.21%. Trading continued to reflect hopes that Saudi Arabia's previously announced partial pipeline restart would ease delivery constraints. That prospective improvement supported prices across financial markets even though Brent remained 14.54% higher over the month. RBC Capital Markets' Blake Gwinn said oil had become a dominant influence on 30-year Treasury yields, with the relationship increasingly reinforcing itself.

Citi analyst Michael Chang also attributed the better bond tone to confidence that the Fed would confront the risk of persistent inflation. Thursday's closing decomposition, however, showed the immediate relief in real borrowing costs: the 10-year TIPS yield fell 7 basis points to 2.61%, while the corresponding breakeven was unchanged at 2.33%. The nominal benchmark's decline therefore matched the fall in its real yield. Inflation compensation had fallen 7 basis points over the week, but did not fall further at Thursday's close.

Demand for new inflation protection was less robust than the nominal rally. The Treasury's $19 billion reopening of 10-year TIPS cleared at 2.653%, about 2 basis points above the yield in pre-auction trading immediately before the 1 p.m. bidding deadline. That tail indicated buyers required additional compensation to absorb the offering. It was the highest auction yield since 2008, compared with 2.438% at the previous sale, but cheaper oil and the prospect of additional Fed increases reduced the attraction of inflation hedges during the session.

The labor figures offered little support for an imminent easing case. Initial unemployment claims fell 10,000 to 196,000 in the week ended September 12, the lowest since mid-July and below the Reuters consensus of 208,000. The four-week average declined 2,750 to 203,250. Continuing claims fell 39,000 to 1.730 million in the week ended September 5, against expectations of 1.780 million and a revised prior level of 1.769 million. That was the lowest continuing-claims reading since January 2024, although Reuters noted that seasonal-adjustment distortions could be influencing the numbers.

Manufacturing was still expanding rapidly in the Philadelphia Fed's September survey, but its composition became less comfortable. The general activity index declined to 37.8 from 47.4, remaining above the 30.5 consensus. New orders eased to 29.2 from 30.1, shipments held at 27.7, and employment fell to 11.8 from 27.9. The average-workweek index was 18.0. Firms were reporting slower expansion rather than an outright contraction, with a much smaller share of the headline strength carrying through to hiring.

Price measures moved in the opposite direction. Prices paid rose to 48.6 from 40.9, and prices received increased about 14 points to 31.3, the highest since April. Future activity dropped to 52.9 from 73.6, while the capital-expenditure index declined to 37.10 from 48.20. Yet future prices-paid and prices-received measures rose to 71.3 and 72.3. Responses collected September 7-15 also showed 72% of firms facing at least a slight labor-supply constraint, up from 50% in June, and 36% expecting energy constraints to worsen over the next three months. The survey combined softer momentum with stronger cost pressure, not a straightforward disinflationary slowdown.

Housing supplied clearer evidence of restraint. August starts fell 2.6% to a 1.275 million annualized rate, below the 1.310 million consensus, as multifamily construction plunged. The prior starts level was revised upward to 1.309 million, with July's monthly decline revised to 9%. Preliminary permits fell 2.7% to 1.394 million from 1.433 million, below the 1.410 million forecast, reversing the previous month's 4.3% increase. Both the activity measure and the permission to undertake future building weakened.

Existing-home contracts improved only modestly. The National Association of Realtors' pending-sales index rose 0.3% to 71.2, its first increase since May, after a revised 2.6% July decline. It exceeded Bloomberg's survey expectation of a 0.1% fall but undershot the separate 2% consensus listed by Trading Economics. Sales remained 4.7% below a year earlier, compared with a previous annual decline of 2.2%. The South, the largest region, gained 2.3%; the West also improved, while the Midwest and Northeast declined. NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun said buyers continued entering contracts despite higher mortgage rates, but activity remained sluggish.

The latest Freddie Mac survey raised the financing hurdle again: the 30-year mortgage rate climbed to 6.95% from 6.76%, and the 15-year rate rose to 6.26% from 6.09%. Those weekly increases sit alongside a daily Treasury rally that only partially unwound the preceding rise in yields. They help explain why a small improvement in contract signings has yet to broaden into stronger construction.

Market volatility was nevertheless considerably calmer than the level of yields might suggest. Reuters reported that three-month options on 10-year U.S. rates implied roughly 79.5 basis points of annualized volatility, against about 134 when the Treasury benchmark approached 5% in October 2023. Barclays strategist Amrut Nashikkar attributed the recent selloff more to stronger growth, a shift from expected cuts to hikes and a higher expected long-run policy rate than to concern over Treasury demand. Options demand was more concentrated in short rates, where uncertainty over the Fed's response remained greater.

Forecasters differed on how durable Thursday's relief would be. BMO Capital Markets' Ian Lyngen expected economic data to regain influence and yields to decline in coming weeks. KKR moved the other way, raising its year-end 10-year forecast to 5.1% from 5.0% and its end-2027 projection to 4.9% from 4.7%. Henry McVey's team still expected Fed increases in December and March, but now anticipated rates staying at those levels through early 2029 rather than 2028, citing persistent inflation, nominal growth, deficits and competition for capital.

Goldman Sachs strategists led by Christian Mueller-Glissman judged that higher starting yields had improved bonds' longer-run income appeal while warning that energy and policy shocks could still make them an unreliable short-term offset to equities. DoubleLine's Jeffrey Gundlach offered a more severe scenario at a New York event: a recession could lift the deficit to 12% of GDP and annual interest expense to roughly $3 trillion, forcing intervention in long rates. He suggested a yield around 6.5% might prompt an Operation Twist-style response and also raised the possibility of coupon reductions, while acknowledging the damage such a restructuring would do to future borrowing. Those were his adverse fiscal scenarios, not announced policy measures.

Thursday's broader markets instead reflected immediate relief. The S&P 500 rose 1.14%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.73%, and semiconductor shares advanced 3.14%. The VIX fell to 15.44, while the Dollar Index edged down 0.07%. Bonds and equities recovered together as lower real yields and cheaper energy eased two pressures on valuations.

## Britain Changes Gilt Supply While Europe Debates Inflation

The Bank of England went substantially beyond the anticipated adjustment to its annual quantitative-tightening pace. It paused all gilt sales until April 2027 and stopped planned sales of long-dated bonds, setting out a route to end the QT program by September 2034. The announcement removed an immediate source of market supply even as the Monetary Policy Committee warned that interest rates might have to rise.

The proposed treatment of its GBP488 billion portfolio distinguishes three groups of assets. Around GBP120 billion maturing in 2049 or later would be retained to back banknotes in circulation. Another GBP222 billion maturing by 2035 would run off. The remaining GBP146 billion, with maturities between 2035 and 2049, would be sold at about GBP20 billion a year, potentially to the Debt Management Office rather than directly into the market. Terms of those transfers still require work and a Treasury decision; the pause provides time to settle them.

The difference is not simply a smaller disposal program. If the DMO acquires and retires the bonds, it could replace them with debt whose maturity better matches demand. Former BOE policymaker Michael Saunders said substituting liquid benchmark issuance for less-liquid, nonbenchmark central-bank sales could produce a more lasting reduction in borrowing costs. Average annual runoff under the proposals would be GBP46 billion, including GBP20 billion of active sales, below the Office for Budget Responsibility's previous assumption of GBP32 billion of annual active disposals.

Gilts reversed earlier losses. The 30-year yield fell 12 basis points to 5.74% in the reported post-decision market, its largest drop since May, while the 2-year declined 6 basis points to 4.70%. Traders reduced anticipated tightening to fewer than four quarter-point increases over the following year. The recovery supported other European bonds, with Germany's 10-year yield down about 3 basis points to 3.48% in the session's reporting.

The fiscal consequences remain more complicated than the market's immediate response. QT has incurred GBP110 billion of losses since 2022 under a Treasury indemnity, after generating GBP124 billion of earlier profits that previous governments spent. The BOE had expected another GBP100 billion of losses. Governor Andrew Bailey said the redesign had been under discussion before the current government took office and would preserve monetary-policy independence. The Treasury believed the changes had little implication for Chancellor John Healey's October 28 budget, according to a person familiar with its assessment, although the arrangements could slightly reduce the cushion under the main fiscal rule.

On rates, the MPC voted 6-3 to hold at 3.75%. Bailey said the energy shock had so far had a limited effect on UK wages and prices, but its persistence would make an increase more likely. The BOE now expects inflation around 4% early next year and raised its Q3 growth forecast to 0.4%. Its minutes warned that indirect energy effects could be delayed rather than smaller, with additional upside risks from food and demand for AI-related products.

Catherine Mann, Megan Greene and Huw Pill again preferred an immediate increase. Their particular concern was that the projected acceleration in prices would coincide with the early-year period when millions of workers negotiate pay. Among the majority, Swati Dhingra and Alan Taylor emphasized labor-market slack and tight financial conditions. Taylor noted that the yield curve was higher than during the 2022-23 cycle, when inflation was close to 7%. Removing gilt supply and keeping the policy rate steady thus addressed different problems: the former eased pressure on the market, while the latter reflected disagreement over whether imported inflation was becoming domestically persistent.

Fresh ECB comments showed a similar distinction without a new policy decision. Ireland's Gabriel Makhlouf said October 29 remained a live meeting and declined either to endorse or dismiss investors' expectations of further increases. He regarded the current 2.5% deposit rate as within the neutral range and saw no concerning wage-driven second-round effects, but stressed that the energy shock was continuing and inflation risks remained on the upside.

Finland's Olli Rehn also reported moderate wage growth and no price-wage spiral so far, while judging last week's increase warranted. He highlighted the tightening already delivered by financial markets as an important policy consideration and warned against broad consumer subsidies that could weaken incentives for the energy transition. Rehn supported joint European borrowing for defense. He said the ECB had instruments, including TPI and OMT, to protect monetary transmission but saw no present need to use them.

Croatia's Ante Zigman put greater emphasis on the risk that uncontrolled inflation would eventually damage growth. Stronger-than-expected Q2 activity gave policymakers reason to concentrate on price stability, he said, while acknowledging that wages and non-energy inflation remained contained. He rejected the view that the ECB was already in its adverse scenario and said October's discussion would depend on data rather than market demands for aggressive tightening. The separate remarks establish a shared concern about persistence but leave room for different judgments on timing.

The Czech National Bank unanimously held at 3.75%, with Governor Ales Michl saying June's increase had tightened conditions sufficiently for now. November's choice would again be between holding and raising rates. He cited services prices, housing, wages and debt-financed government spending alongside energy risks, with persistent core inflation requiring continued restraint despite below-target August headline inflation. Forward-rate agreements incorporated roughly two further quarter-point increases this year and four over the next 12 months; Michl said domestic market rates were being strongly influenced by U.S. policy and declined to validate that path.

Food added a fresh estimate to the inflation debate. JPMorgan economists forecast global food inflation of 5% in H1 2027, up from 2.8% in H1 2026, while a UN food-commodity index was at its highest since late 2022. Carmignac's Marie-Anne Allier expected a slow but persistent supply shock from weather, fertilizer constraints and shipping disruption. A new Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit analysis estimated that heat and drought could reduce Europe's and the UK's potato crop by about 3.5 million tons, costing farmers more than EUR800 million at current prices; reported yield losses reached 21% in Belgium, 13% in France and 10% in Germany.

JPMorgan Asset Management's Karen Ward offered an important counterargument: more expensive essentials depress spending elsewhere, and labor markets in Europe and the United States might not support sustained wage pass-through. The distinction matters after a day when oil eased but central banks continued to worry about the duration and breadth of supply pressure. The new food estimates concern the coming months, not a realized increase in Thursday's inflation data.

Trade policy introduced another potential cost shock. Trump threatened new tariffs or restrictions on European trade if the EU's proposed association with Canada proved hostile to U.S. interests, while Mark Carney welcomed closer ties in Thursday's European Parliament speech. Congress also gave final approval to legislation granting new powers to impose tariffs on buyers of Russian petroleum. Neither development established a new tariff rate. Separately, people familiar with the matter said a U.S. announcement on excess-capacity tariffs was expected to wait until after the Trump-Xi summit, with the eventual rate still uncertain.

## Banks Find Buyers as AI Borrowers Diversify Funding

Citigroup raised $12 billion in its largest dollar bond sale, drawing about $40 billion of peak orders as lower Treasury yields improved issuance conditions. Its 11-year tranche priced at 0.93 percentage point above the benchmark, compared with initial discussions around 1.25 percentage points. That maturity attracted roughly $18 billion of demand, the largest order book among the deal's tranches.

Wells Fargo also completed a $6 billion offering in four- and 11-year notes, with about $28 billion of peak demand. The transactions lifted the six largest U.S. banks' combined investment-grade issuance this year to $177.3 billion. Citi's total reached $18.3 billion and Wells Fargo's $24 billion, compared with Goldman Sachs' $44 billion. There were six high-grade offerings on Thursday, bringing weekly issuance close to dealer expectations.

The concentration of Citi orders in its longest tranche supplied fresh evidence of demand for duration at an acceptable issuer spread. Borrowers have been reluctant to lock in expensive long-term funding, leaving investors competing for the maturities that do come to market. Thursday's transactions showed that a higher Fed rate need not close the primary market when government yields retreat and investors remain willing to accept corporate risk.

U.S. high-yield spreads tightened modestly over the session. The investment-grade fund LQD returned about 0.68%, while HYG gained 0.38% and the emerging-market debt fund EMB advanced 0.64%. The recovery in traded debt coincided with continued differentiation in the terms offered to AI-infrastructure borrowers.

CoreWeave launched a proposed $3 billion senior convertible issue due in 2033, with an option to increase it by $500 million. Initial coupon indications were 2.375%-2.875%. Proceeds would support general corporate purposes and derivative agreements associated with the transaction. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo were working on the offering, which was expected to price later Thursday.

The company simultaneously established an at-the-market program allowing sales of as many as 35 million shares over time. CoreWeave said that flexibility would help move its credit profile toward investment grade. The combination adds possible equity issuance to debt that can itself convert into shares, broadening funding beyond conventional loans and bonds. U.S.-listed companies had already raised a record $137.3 billion through convertible securities this year, while AI-related companies' global borrowing had reached about $419 billion.

CleanSpark sought roughly $2.23 billion in a debut high-yield offering for a data center in Sandersville, Georgia. Initial discussion for the five-year bonds was around an 8.5% yield, about 2 percentage points above the average for BB debt tracked by Bloomberg. Orders were roughly equal to the deal's size when it launched Thursday. Morgan Stanley led the financing, with Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo also underwriting, and pricing was expected Friday.

The project is fully leased to Meta subsidiary Anviran under a $6.6 billion, 20-year agreement, with Meta guaranteeing rent and operating expenses. Operations are expected to begin in Q4 2027. The contract gives CleanSpark a long revenue commitment, but investors were still demanding a substantial yield for financing construction before those payments support an operating facility. It is the first U.S. junk-bond offering tied to a Meta data center; developers have sold about $39 billion of high-yield debt this year, much of it supported by hyperscaler leases.

Chip purchases are creating additional borrowing needs in Asia. Nvidia partner GMI Cloud was discussing a $300 million loan with banks and private-credit funds to buy processors for a Thai facility whose computing capacity would be used by Tencent, according to people familiar with the talks. The prospective financing places the equipment inside the building at the center of the lending decision.

The demand for electricity accompanying that investment is also expanding financing beyond technology issuers. BloombergNEF research published Thursday found that banks arranged and underwrote $2.3 trillion of energy-sector transactions in 2025, 15% more than in 2024. Low-carbon financing increased 16% to a five-year high, while oil, gas and coal transactions rose 13%. The study describes the previous year's funding, with significant regional differences and Wall Street banks trailing European counterparts in low-carbon financing.

Outside AI, Pizza Hut was preparing bonds backed by franchise fees to finance LongRange Capital's $1.5 billion buyout. UBS supplied the funding and was expected to lead the whole-business securitization after rating agencies assess the debt. The acquisition closed earlier this month. The structure can reduce financing costs by separating pledged operating cash flows into a special-purpose vehicle, but restaurant performance remains consequential: FAT Brands filed for bankruptcy in January after missing interest on some of its $1.2 billion of whole-business securitizations. Pizza Hut's proposed transaction had not yet launched.

## Debt Workouts Expose Cash-Flow and Valuation Gaps

Braskem's restructuring talks deteriorated as bondholders resisted a proposal requiring them to contribute about $2 billion of new money without the enforceable shareholder capital commitment they wanted. The dispute concerns an $11 billion debt pile, roughly $7 billion of which is owed to bondholders, and has brought judicial reorganization back into the negotiations.

Under the proposal presented in late August, about $1.25 billion of creditor funding would repurchase existing debt at as much as 50% of face value, with $750 million left for working capital. That represents a departure from initial discussions that did not contemplate a haircut. Creditors objected after Petrobras and IG4 Capital softened language around a capital injection; some were considering withholding a counterproposal entirely.

Petrobras wants to avoid a Braskem bankruptcy but has not offered the binding commitment sought by lenders, according to people familiar with the talks. Some creditors no longer regard a possible follow-on equity offering as sufficient. The parties have until October 9 to agree on a term sheet, and Braskem has until late November to secure a final plan supported by more than half its creditors. Its 2030 dollar notes yielded about 26%. The immediate obstacle is who supplies dependable new capital, not merely how far existing maturities can be extended.

In Australia, Centuria Bass Credit explored selling part of its exposure to insolvent builder Bathla, with prospective buyers seeking discounts of at least 20%-30%, according to people familiar with the discussions. No transaction was imminent, and the manager declined to comment on potential discounts. It had disclosed A$278 million of Bathla debt secured on six residential projects in Victoria and New South Wales and temporarily paused redemptions in two funds.

Bathla owes about A$3.4 billion, largely to private-credit lenders. Administrator Teneo has obtained roughly A$4 million of emergency financing and is seeking a broader package. Higher construction and borrowing costs have coincided with weaker sales and property prices, leaving the manager's proposed asset sale dependent on what outside buyers will pay. The potential discounts are bids for exposure, not settled recovery values.

French property-services company Emeria brought the definition of earnings into its own debt discussions. It added EUR20 million of anticipated savings from agentic AI to last-twelve-month EBITDA for the period ended June 30, drawing on estimated efficiency gains over the next two years. Emeria said these reflected identified actions in document preparation, customer service, accounting and back-office automation, and were consistent with lender-agreed methodology. The adjustment had not been audited or reviewed by its independent auditors and remained subject to change.

The company reported leverage of about 8.44 times pro forma adjusted EBITDA. Bloomberg calculated a ratio nearer 9.3 times without the AI adjustment and several other items totaling roughly EUR40 million. Emeria has about EUR3.5 billion of debt and is discussing a possible EUR350 million sponsor injection as earnings weaken and maturities approach. Spread Research's Benjamin Sabahi argued that prospective AI savings should count only once generated; other market participants likened them to conventional operational-efficiency adjustments. Emeria emphasized that it disclosed each adjustment separately so lenders could form their own assessments.

A new comparison of private-credit distress gauges showed a similar dependence on definitions. Houlihan Lokey's loan-size-weighted default measure remained below 1%, reflecting continued performance among the largest borrowers. Pimco's shadow-default gauge for the approximately $500 billion U.S. business-development-company market instead stood at 19%, up from about 14% in 2022. It includes payment-in-kind terms added after origination to relieve cash-flow pressure, rather than PIK provisions built into the original financing.

That distinction explains part of the gap with the previously reported 6.3% Fitch default rate and with Lincoln International's 1.5% measure for European loans, which excludes some such events. Credit Benchmark research added another comparison: over the past two years, average BDC risk declined 5% while default risk in their underlying holdings increased 12%. Pimco's Lotfi Karoui said non-accrual measures alone could miss restructurings that postpone recognition of stress. The studies cover different borrowers and events, but collectively expose why continued interest accrual can coexist with deteriorating repayment capacity.

ING strategist Timothy Rahill estimated that managers could absorb default rates of 8%-9% in highly leveraged portfolios, while a rise toward 12%-15% after a major shock would raise systemic questions. Those thresholds are his assessment of potential loss absorption, distinct from Pimco's broader measure of modified loans. Negotiations, payment deferrals and outright defaults carry different cash consequences even when grouped under the same headline.

Fund liquidity supplied two other developments. Investors withdrew more than $530 million from the roughly $3.6 billion Schwab Municipal Bond ETF during September, including a record $360 million in one day last week. Schwab owns just over half the shares, leading Bloomberg Intelligence's Eric Balchunas to suspect model-portfolio rebalancing. That explanation differs from widespread municipal-credit deterioration, even as higher Treasury rates and heavy supply have pressured tax-exempt bonds.

Turkey's regulators, meanwhile, moved from the preceding redemption disruption to plans to liquidate about $20 billion of funds run by Tera Portfoy and other managers. Authorities filed criminal complaints and imposed trading bans over alleged share-price manipulation; some executives were detained and others faced travel restrictions. Tera managed roughly TRY730 billion, or $15 billion, and some affected funds had concentrated positions in illiquid shares. The broad equity index steadied after a three-day decline of almost 10%, but liquidation now makes the disposal of those holdings a concrete local-market issue.

## Sovereign Funding and Asian Policy Diverge

India's Reserve Bank completed the first INR500 billion installment of its announced bond-sale program, turning a prospective liquidity withdrawal into an actual operation. It was the first auction-based net open-market sale since November 2017 and covered maturities from 2029 to 2032, with cutoff prices between INR102.25 and INR105.63. The sale absorbed nearly 0.2% of banking-system deposits.

Five-year yields rose as much as 6 basis points to 6.83% after the results, exceeding the benchmark 10-year's increase of as much as 3 basis points. The shorter sector had benefited most from banks investing surplus liquidity and was more exposed to its removal. Reuters put the surplus at INR7.4 trillion after a September 6 record of INR11.6 trillion, with tax outflows and foreign-exchange intervention contributing to the reduction. Further INR250 billion sales are scheduled for September 21 and 28, ahead of the October 7 policy review.

India also outlined a longer-term financing initiative. SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey supported pooled municipal borrowing to help smaller towns access the bond market, building on a May consultation. NaBFID chief Rajkiran Rai G. said urban infrastructure could require INR82 trillion-INR86 trillion by fiscal 2031, roughly $855 billion-$900 billion. Only 22 local bodies had raised more than INR45 billion through 31 municipal issues through the year ended March. Pandey emphasized creditworthiness, governance, disclosure and dependable project cash flow as the conditions for expansion.

Malaysia faced a different funding pressure from the narrowing return advantage over Japan. Its 10-year sovereign premium over comparable Japanese bonds had compressed to about 112 basis points, against a five-year average of 278. Japanese investors held JPY1.1 trillion of Malaysian debt at end-2025, a record in data beginning in 2014 and 13% of their Asian bond holdings. CIMB's Michelle Chia said higher JGB yields increased the opportunity cost of overseas duration and the risk of capital returning home.

Domestic repricing compounded that exposure. Malaysian swaps incorporated nearly 50 basis points of tightening over the next year, compared with less than 25 at end-August, while the 10-year yield had risen 51 basis points since June. Authorities announced another MYR5 billion of debt due in 2033 on Thursday. Higher fuel subsidies, robust growth and inflation risks added to the supply and external-rate pressures, according to BNP Paribas' Chandresh Jain.

Japan's own financing base showed a substantial change. Retail JGB sales for April-September reached a record JPY5.14 trillion, up 84% from a year earlier. Households held JPY1,132 trillion in cash and deposits, compared with government-bond holdings equivalent to just 1.9% of that amount. Bloomberg's comparison estimated that a return to the 2008 peak ratio of 4.5% could imply another JPY28.5 trillion of purchases, equivalent to 22% of fiscal-year government issuance. That is a potential reallocation, not an announced household commitment.

Retail bonds offer a JPY10,000 minimum and yields above time deposits, though below comparable marketable JGBs. The Finance Ministry plans to expand eligibility to nonprofit entities and small unlisted companies later this year. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama has proposed including government bonds in NISA, while legislation submitted to the upper house would exempt some retail issues from inheritance tax. Barclays' Shinichiro Kadota said greater household demand could reduce the supply institutional investors must absorb as the BOJ scales back purchases.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi retained Katayama and economic revitalization minister Minoru Kiuchi in Thursday's reshuffle. Kiuchi promised clearer communication on public finances and said the government's pursuit of stronger growth did not imply unchecked fiscal expansion. That assurance accompanied continuity in the officials responsible for fiscal and currency policy, rather than a new spending package.

Other Asian economies supplied reasons not to follow U.S. tightening mechanically. Bank of Thailand Assistant Governor Don Nakornthab described the 1.00% policy rate as highly accommodative for a weak economy and said all options remained open. He retained growth forecasts of 2.3% for 2026 and 1.8% for 2027, expecting Q3 growth above 3% before a slowdown toward 2% in Q4. Inflation was expected to average around 2% this year, below June's 2.8% forecast, while exports could exceed the bank's 14% growth estimate. He saw no apparent immediate impact from the Fed move and no need to match it.

Singapore's electronics exports rose 132% from a year earlier in August, including increases of 238% in personal computers, 214% in disk drives and 91% in integrated circuits. Barclays raised its 2026 and 2027 growth forecasts by 1 percentage point each, to 5.5% and 4%, yet economist Brian Tan forecast core inflation of only 1.7%. He argued that higher capacity utilization rather than hiring was driving the capital-intensive boom, while foreign firms would likely repatriate profits rather than distribute large local wage gains.

Tan expected only slight additional MAS tightening, mainly because of commodity and weather risks, and regarded a hold as a substantial possibility. Maybank's Chua Hak Bin and Brian Lee expected no October change after the April and July adjustments, which they estimated had steepened the policy band by a combined 75 basis points. OCBC's Selena Ling said another move would likely require upside risk to the 2027 core-inflation outlook. The export release raised growth forecasts without producing equivalent agreement on stronger domestic price pressure.

China's low-cost funding channels continued to offer alternatives. In a new interview, Hong Kong Green Finance Association chairman Ma Jun put mainland panda issuance over the preceding eight months at about CNY200 billion. He cited Pakistan's 2.5% panda coupon, explicitly supported by AIIB and ADB guarantees, as an example of the financing advantage for green projects. He also described a newly launched Hong Kong Green Accelerator intended to prepare bankable projects in developing economies, with participants including AIIB, the Silk Road Fund, GenZero and HSBC. The initiative targets project preparation as well as capital provision; Ma estimated that local emerging-market banks reject 90% of proposed green projects.

Sovereign dollar performance elsewhere was highly country-specific. Mozambique's bonds returned about 3% in September and Senegal's 2.2%, against a 1.23% loss for an emerging-market bond index. Mozambique's $900 million 2031 issue yielded 10.43% at 2:20 p.m. Thursday in London, down 76 basis points over the month and its lowest since April 2022. Aquila's Manuel Mondia cited the tone of IMF talks, discussions with China about rescheduling debt and tentative bondholder restructuring proposals.

Senegal's recovery followed clarification that debt service would continue for now and payment of the coupon on its 2048 bonds, according to Standard Chartered's Samir Gadio. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye had completed Tuesday's meeting with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, while board approval for the $2.2 billion program remained pending. The new payment and negotiation developments supported a partial price recovery without resolving the external debt treatment.

Peru's Senate confirmed Julio Velarde for another five-year term following President Keiko Fujimori's request that he remain central-bank governor. His reappointment preserves monetary leadership in place since 2006 and removes an immediate succession uncertainty. In Canada, the government sold C$3 billion of bonds due June 1, 2059, at an average 4.201% yield, the highest for a Canadian 30-year auction since July 2007. The completed sale demonstrated the elevated cost of securing long-term funds even during a day of improving global bond prices.

The European Commission addressed demand rather than auction terms, pledging to press for EU bonds' inclusion in major sovereign indexes. Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said their exclusion constrained demand and liquidity despite roughly EUR800 billion outstanding and secondary-market liquidity comparable with large European sovereigns. The bonds already receive sovereign-equivalent collateral treatment at clearing houses and in ECB refinancing operations. Wider index recognition would matter as common borrowing expands, including financing associated with the next long-term EU budget, but inclusion remains a policy objective rather than a completed benchmark change.

## Forward Market Significance

The BOJ's September 18 decision is the nearest policy test. All economists in Bloomberg's survey expect an increase from 1.00% to 1.25%, with Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference scheduled for 3:30 p.m. Japan time. Attention is therefore on whether he presents a faster continuing pace or a one-off acceleration. A move to 1.25% would enter the lower end of the BOJ's estimated neutral range; retaining the description of financial conditions as accommodative would leave room for further tightening. The votes of Takaichi appointees Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato will also help establish the breadth of support.

That guidance now faces a higher U.S. rate path and a renewed yen challenge. SMBC Nikko's Rinto Maruyama judged that a dovish interpretation could take dollar-yen toward 158, while ACCM's Glenn Yin warned that 160 could not be dismissed if the BOJ disappointed. Recent reductions in speculative yen shorts and the possibility of renewed intervention are counterweights. For bond markets, the combination of greater Japanese household demand and a much narrower Malaysian yield premium makes the relative attraction of domestic and overseas duration particularly consequential.

U.S. industrial production on September 18 will follow Philadelphia's combination of slower activity and rising costs. Consensus calls for a 0.3% August increase, after 0.2%, with manufacturing output also expected to rise 0.3% and capacity utilization to reach 76.4% from 76.3%. Michelle Bowman's scheduled remarks that day provide an opportunity to assess how the latest labor and manufacturing evidence affects the policy judgment. ADP's weekly employment estimate on September 22 and the September 23 S&P Global flash composite PMI extend that test to fresh hiring and a broader activity survey.

Energy risks remain capable of interrupting the relief. Trump told Axios he was approaching a decision on renewed attacks against Iran ahead of meetings with Gulf leaders at the United Nations the following week. JPMorgan oil analysts said the path to an end to the conflict had become increasingly difficult to predict. The threat of renewed escalation now sits against Thursday's lower crude prices, while the BOE's new inflation forecast and the Philadelphia survey show why the duration of elevated costs matters beyond the next daily oil move.

CleanSpark's expected Friday pricing will give a direct test of the 8.5% initial yield discussion for a construction-stage project with Meta-backed rent. Braskem's October 9 term-sheet deadline poses a different financing question: whether shareholders will make a binding contribution sufficient to keep the restructuring out of court. Britain's Treasury, meanwhile, must decide how the proposed DMO transfers will work. Finalizing that arrangement would determine how much of Thursday's immediate gilt relief becomes a durable change in the maturity and liquidity of debt reaching investors.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries end an eight-session yield rise as cheaper oil and a gilt recovery ease pressure
overall_summary.session_narrative:
The 10-year Treasury yield fell 7 basis points to 4.94%, ending eight consecutive increases, and the 2-year declined by the same amount to 4.67%. Cheaper oil and a sharp gilt recovery supported the move after the Fed's inflation-fighting message. The decline in the 10-year nominal yield matched a fall in its real yield; inflation compensation was unchanged. This was relief in borrowing costs, not an abandonment of further tightening expectations.

The Bank of England supplied the main policy surprise, pausing gilt sales until April 2027 and stopping planned long-dated disposals while holding its policy rate at 3.75%. The immediate reduction in supply supported bonds beyond Britain, although the proposed transfers to the Debt Management Office still require a Treasury decision. U.S. data offered a mixed backdrop: initial claims fell to 196,000, Philadelphia manufacturers reported stronger price pressures, and housing starts and permits weakened.

Financing remained available at differentiated terms. Citigroup completed a record $12 billion dollar sale with about $40 billion of peak orders. CoreWeave proposed convertible debt alongside potential equity sales, while CleanSpark sought an initial yield around 8.5% for a construction-stage data center with Meta-guaranteed rent. Active issuance therefore coexisted with a substantial price for project risk. Renewed threats of attacks on Iran left the durability of the oil-led relief uncertain.
